question.text: The value of $p$ and $q$ for which the function $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cl}\frac{\sin (p+1) x+\sin x}{x} & x < 0 \\ q & , x=0 \\ \frac{\sqrt{x+x^2}-\sqrt{x}}{x^{3 / 2}} & , x>0\end{array}\right.$ is continuous for all $\mathrm{x}$ in $\mathrm{R}$, is

solution.text:
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin (p+1)+\sin x}{x}=q=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sqrt{x+x^2}-\sqrt{x}}{x^{3 / 2}}$
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}(p+1) \cos (p+1) x+\cos x=q=\frac{1}{2}$
$\Rightarrow p+1+1=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow p=-\frac{3}{2} ; q=\frac{1}{2}$
